lead.tldr: Senate compromise bans deposit‑like stablecoin yields, forces shift to use‑based rewards, crypto groups endorse markup • Final CLARITY Act rules provide clear guidance for stablecoin interest products, potentially unlocking broader market adoption • Ethereum Foundation's third ETH sale to BitMine signals cash‑flow pressure, while BitMine's staked holdings near five million • April venture capital hit $600 m, with Kraken’s $200 m secondary sale indicating continued liquidity appetite • Bitcoin climbs to $73,600, yet options pricing assigns low probability to $84,000, urging cautious positioning

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, the CLARITY Act compromise clears a path for crypto yield, $600 M of VC funding landed in April, and Riot’s mining revenue hit $167 M in Q1. Ethereum’s $23 M ETH sale and the rise of open‑source AI platforms like Sentient underline ecosystem shifts.

top_signals.title: Crypto industry backs CLARITY Act yield compromise, pushes Senate Banking for markup
top_signals.summary: U.S. Senators Thom Tillis and Angela Alsobrooks have issued a compromise amendment to the CLARITY Act that prohibits stablecoin yield products that replicate traditional bank deposits while allowing rewards linked to legitimate usage activities. The proposal has been quickly endorsed by major crypto trade groups such as Coinbase and Circle, which are urging the Senate Banking Committee to advance the legislation to a markup. Under the compromise, firms must redesign reward programs from a “buy‑and‑hold” structure to a “buy‑and‑use” model that ties earnings to actual token utility. The Crypto Council for Innovation cautioned that the language of the amendment may be overly broad, a point that institutional investors will watch closely as it could affect the design of compliant stablecoin offerings.

top_signals.title: CLARITY Act Stablecoin Yield Rules Finalized: ‘Go Time’ For Crypto Bill
top_signals.summary: The U.S. CLARITY Act has finalized its stablecoin yield rules, delivering clear regulatory guidance for crypto yield products. This clarification removes a key source of uncertainty for institutional investors who want to offer or invest in interest‑bearing stablecoin services. By signaling a green light for the industry, the rules are expected to unlock broader adoption of stablecoin‑based interest products across the financial sector.

top_signals.title: Ethereum Foundation Offloads $23M in ETH to BitMine for Third Time in Two Months
top_signals.summary: The Ethereum Foundation transferred 10,000 ETH, valued at approximately $23 million, to the mining pool BitMine, marking its third ETH sale within a two‑month window. This transaction follows an earlier unstaking event in which the foundation sold 17,035 ETH for roughly $40 million. The repeated off‑loading has attracted criticism from the Ethereum community and prompted questions about the foundation’s liquidity requirements. BitMine’s holdings now approach 5 million ETH and the firm is steadily raising the share of its portfolio that is actively staked, a trend that may affect staking yields and network security.

top_signals.title: Crypto companies raised $600m in April despite despite market downturn, VCs say
top_signals.summary: Crypto startups raised just over $600 million in venture funding in April, a 75 percent drop from the previous month but still a notable inflow amid a broader market downturn. The largest transaction was a $200 million secondary share sale by Kraken to Deutsche Börse. Additional significant rounds included a $100 million Series C for neobanking platform Slash and a $44 million raise by Pharos for its Layer‑1 blockchain, highlighting continued investor focus on core infrastructure and financial services in the crypto sector.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin Rally Accelerates, But BTC Options Doubt $84K Is Possible
top_signals.summary: Bitcoin rallied to around $73,600, accelerating its recent price gains. Options market data shows traders assigning a low probability to the price reaching the $84,000 level, indicating skepticism despite the upward momentum. This divergence between spot price strength and derivative pricing may prompt institutional investors to weigh momentum against downside risk.

top_signals.title: Riot Posts $167M in Q1 Revenue as Data Center Arm Pulls in $33M
top_signals.summary: Riot Platforms announced total revenue of $167 million for the first quarter. The revenue was generated primarily from its Bitcoin mining operations. Within the quarter, the company’s data‑center division contributed $33 million. This contribution highlights the ongoing expansion of Riot’s mining infrastructure, a key metric for investors assessing the firm’s scale and operational efficiency.

top_signals.title: SENT - Sentient - AMBCrypto
top_signals.summary: Sentient is building an open‑source, community‑driven artificial general intelligence platform named the Sentient GRID, which aims to serve as a decentralized alternative to traditional closed AI laboratories. The project’s native token, SENT, is currently trading at approximately $0.015 and carries a market capitalization of about $108 million. SENT is listed on major cryptocurrency exchanges including Binance, Toobit, and Bybit, providing institutional investors with accessible liquidity and exposure to the emerging decentralized AI sector.

top_signals.title: TAG - TAGGER - AMBCrypto
top_signals.summary: Tagger (ticker TAG) operates a decentralized full‑stack AI data platform that allows permissionless collection, labeling, authentication and trading of data. The platform’s token is currently priced around $0.0012 and the market capitalization stands at approximately $132.75 million. This valuation provides institutional investors with measurable liquidity while the protocol’s infrastructure supports AI model development across multiple sectors. Although the token experienced a modest decline over the past 24 hours, its year‑to‑date growth remains strong, indicating continued market interest.

linkedin_post: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, The past weeks have delivered a clear signal that the crypto ecosystem is moving from uncertainty to execution. Senators Thom Tillis and Angela Alsobrooks have introduced a compromise amendment to the CLARITY Act that bans stablecoin yield products that simply mimic bank deposits while rewarding users for genuine on‑chain activity. Major players such as Coinbase and Circle have already voiced support and are urging the Senate Banking Committee to move the bill forward. The Crypto Council for Innovation warned that the language could be broader than intended, a point that institutional investors will monitor closely as they redesign reward programs from a buy‑and‑hold to a buy‑and‑use model. At the same time, the CLARITY Act has finalized its stablecoin yield rules, delivering the “go time” many have awaited. With clear guidance in place, institutional capital can now consider interest‑bearing stablecoin services without the cloud of regulatory doubt, opening the door for broader adoption across the financial sector. In parallel, the Ethereum Foundation has transferred another 10,000 ETH, worth about $23 million, to mining pool BitMine, its third sale in two months. The repeated off‑loading follows a larger sale earlier this year and has sparked debate about the foundation’s liquidity strategy. BitMine’s growing stake in active ETH further highlights the evolving dynamics of staking yields and network security.
